learning: Iterations 0 to 6 show pitch, footprint, track, gains, mass and wheel_radius each leave max_error at the 0.06 m floor and one line loss per run. Wheel_radius 0.035 gave no progress gain (iteration 6). If line_loss_events falls to 0 with max_error below 0.06 m, lag was the limit. If the loss persists with no max_error change, the controller rather than the geometry is the next suspect.
notes: Sensor-lead test: the iteration 5 geometry with the sensor bar moved to y = 0.06 m and wheel_radius reverted to 0.030 m, as the Builder requested. The controller is unchanged from iterations 5 and 6 so the race isolates lead. Controller_errors and control_effort are requested to catch integration faults.
rationale: Iterations 0 to 6 (420 trials, all off_track) show max_error pinned at the 0.060 to 0.068 m off-track floor and one line-loss event per run from iteration 3 onward. Pitch (10 to 20 mm), footprint (12 to 16 mm), track (0.12 to 0.10 m), kp (1.2 to 1.4), mass (0.8 to 0.4 kg) and wheel_radius (0.030 to 0.035 m) each left these unchanged. Iteration 6 raised wheel_radius with no progress gain (0.10 to 0.16 band), so the speed hypothesis is weakened. The Builder's entity0 moves the sensor bar forward from y = 0.04 m to y = 0.06 m, the only geometry change from iteration 5 apart from reverting wheel_radius to 0.030 m. I build exactly that geometry: x = -0.04 to +0.04 at 20 mm pitch, sensor_size 0.016, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.030 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m, mass 0.4 kg. The controller is held at the iteration 5 and 6 values (kp 1.4, ki 0.05, kd 0.15, base_speed 1.6, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction) so any change is attributable to sensor lead. Expected: line_loss_events toward 0 and max_error below about 0.06 m, but I make no claim about the outcome, since nothing has raced for this design.
